methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 195 male HCC patients with standardized CT-based L3-SMI measurement segmented by SliceOmatic with dual radiologist review and adjudication. Strengths include defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and adjustment for age. Weaknesses include male-only inclusion limiting generalizability, only ~29 deaths at 12 months (15% cumulative), and a multivariate HR of 0.02 with 95% CI 0.001–0.940 that indicates instability. Optimal cut-offs for each SMI are derived data-driven (surv_cutpoint) without correction for multiple testing or internal validation. SHAP and ROC AUC of 0.86 are presented without bootstrap CIs for discrimination or calibration.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Skeletal muscle indices are clinically relevant in HCC immunotherapy, and L3-SMI/BMI could be operationalized from routine CT. However, the single-center, male-only, predominantly BCLC A/B cohort and event-sparse analysis restrict applicability. The LoE maps to a low-quality cohort (Oxford 4) given retrospective design and selection restrictions.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic/prediction-oriented study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard. Many items are addressed (source of data, participants, predictor definitions, outcomes, statistical methods, performance metrics), but key TRIPOD elements are missing: no sample-size justification, no internal validation (bootstrap/cross-validation), no calibration assessment, no full model specification (coefficients), and no risk-of-bias discussion. No data/code availability statement; several URLs are [REDACTED].

novelty_literature.justification: Applying L3-SMI/BMI specifically in male HCC patients on ICIs adds to a growing literature on sarcopenia and immunotherapy outcomes. The comparison across four SMI variants (L3-SMI, /weight, /height, /BMI) is a useful refinement but not a fundamentally new concept, as SMI/BMI has been favored for metabolic syndrome and heart failure. This represents meaningful incremental extension rather than a first-in-class finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is clearly organized with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and figures/tables are referenced. Language is mostly clear, with occasional awkwardness ('Relevance of multiple SMIs'), and a few typographic/grammatical issues. The [REDACTED] placeholders interrupt reading. Overall an adequate but not polished manuscript.

key_strengths: Standardized L3 CT segmentation with dual radiologist review
Head-to-head comparison of four skeletal muscle indices including L3-SMI/BMI
Reasonable event-based outcome (1-year OS) with SHAP and ROC analyses
key_concerns: Multivariate HR 0.02 with 95% CI 0.001–0.940 suggests unstable effect estimates in a small-event setting
Data-driven optimal cut-offs used without correction or internal validation
Male-only, single-center, BCLC A/B-dominant cohort limits generalizability
Key TRIPOD items (calibration, internal validation, full model equation) not reported
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective prognostic study whose statistical fragility and restricted cohort fit a Tier 3 specialty journal pending major TRIPOD-aligned revisions and internal validation.
